subject: Clarify term, auto-renew and TFC windows — redline collaboration for ACME order form
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.io>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed redlines on Term + Auto‑Renew + TFC (ACME)

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking this through — attached is ACME's consolidated redline of the MSA and the Order Form. High level asks are:

- Limit initial term to 12 months with option to renew annually (no automatic multi‑year roll).
- Auto‑renew: move from auto‑renew by default to "requires affirmative renewal" unless we sign 30 days prior to expiration.
- Notice window: ACME requests a 60‑day notice for non‑renewal instead of Redwood's standard 30 days.
- Termination for convenience (TFC): request a 90‑day wind‑down plus prorated refund for pre‑paid services; alternatively a mutual TFC with no fees.

We put comments inline in the attached Redline_MSA_v3.docx and flagged the OrderForm for billing cadence adjustments.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on the notice window and whether the TFC refundable model is acceptable? Jordan and I are on a fairly tight procurement timeline (legal needs final language by EOD next Tuesday).

Thanks,
Alicia

[Attachment: Redline_MSA_v3.docx (docx)]
[Attachment: ACME_OrderForm_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.io>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines on Term + Auto‑Renew + TFC (ACME)

Alicia —

Appreciate the clear notes and the redline. Quick read-through from my side:

- Term: 12‑month initial term is fine from a commercial perspective; we prefer a default annual auto‑renew to avoid service interruption, but open to a minimum 30‑day affirmative renewal window if that's a hard ACME constraint.
- Auto‑renew vs affirmative: If ACME insists on affirmative renewal, we need firm language around a short grace/breach window so heavy production customers don't accidentally lapse. We can agree to a 30‑day affirmative window (rather than 60) if we can keep the auto‑renew for customers with prepayment.
- Notice window: 60 days is larger than standard — operationally the 30‑day notice is important for capacity planning. We can offer a 45‑day notice for enterprise SKUs as a middle ground.
- TFC: 90‑day wind‑down and prorated refund is a fair ask for a pilot or prepaid agreement. For committed/discounted order forms we typically do the 90‑day wind‑down but not full refunds on committed spend.

Looping in Karthik and Laura to confirm legal/procurement tolerances before we send a track‑changed counter. Marissa, if you can weigh in on whether the affirmative renewal language or the 45‑day compromise is acceptable from a risk standpoint that would help.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood sends a clean counter with 12‑month initial term, 45‑day notice, and a TFC option that differentiates between prepaid pilots (prorated refund) and committed deals (90‑day wind‑down, no refund).
2) ACME reviews and we aim to lock the MSA language in 2 business days.

Ben
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.io>, Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.io>
Date: Fri, 08 Oct 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposed redlines on Term + Auto‑Renew + TFC (ACME)

Ben/Karthik/Laura —

Thanks for the summary. From a legal/commercial risk perspective here's a recommended compromise we can live with (I also attached a draft counter redline):

- Term: Keep 12‑month initial term with automatic 12‑month renewals unless Customer provides written non‑renewal notice within the Notice Window.
- Notice Window: Set at 45 days for standard Order Forms; allow 60 days as a negotiable option for customers contracting for >$1M annual committed spend. Reason: 45 days balances procurement needs with our capacity planning and billing cycles.
- Auto‑renew affirmative carve: Add a carve for "prepaid pilots" — those require affirmative renewal to be replicated in the Order Form. Wording: "For prepaid or pilot Order Forms explicitly designated as 'Pilot — affirmative renewal required', this Order Form will not auto‑renew and Customer must provide written renewal notice at least 30 days prior to Term end."
- TFC (Termination for Convenience): 90‑day wind‑down for all Order Forms. Refund mechanics: For month‑to‑month or prepaid pilots, Customer receives a prorated refund of unused prepaid fees. For committed discounted orders, Customer receives a credit equal to the unused portion of services (no cash refund), and Redwood retains the right to apply termination fees if there is evidence of early termination intended to avoid committed spend.

Key redline language I recommend adding (in plain text to insert):
"If termination for convenience is exercised by Customer, Redwood will provide 90 days' written notice period for orderly wind‑down of services. For prepaid Pilot Orders, Redwood will issue a prorated refund for unused prepaid fees within 30 days of termination. For committed discounted Orders, Redwood will calculate an unused services credit and apply against outstanding charges; no cash refunds will be issued except at Redwood's discretion."

I attached the tracked redline for the MSA (Redline_MSA_v3_docx_counter.docx) and a one‑page summary. If you want a slightly tighter legal posture, we can make the 45‑day window non‑negotiable for < $1M deals and 60 days only available as an explicit procurement concession.

I'll join any call if ACME wants to walk through language.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.io>

Cc: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Oct 2026 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines on Term + Auto‑Renew + TFC (ACME)

Thanks everyone — the Marissa draft reads reasonable and gets us most of the protections we need. A couple of small asks before legal will sign off:

- Could we move the 45‑day notice to 50 days? ACME procurement uses a 50‑day internal cutoff and it's a hard constraint when coordinating finance + cloud migration windows.
- For prepaid pilots, can the prorated refund be disbursed within 21 days instead of 30? Our accounting team prefers a faster close on pilot refunds.

If Redwood is okay with those two small changes, we can proceed to DocuSign. We're aiming to have counters signed and DocuSigned by Wednesday COB.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Alicia
Director, Strategic Procurement
Acme Cloudware
